column1: # boru Language Specification: codequote (structural paren quotability)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# `codequote` is `quote`'s code-capturing sibling. It captures a forward
# PAREN raw — as a ParenExpr value (code/data) — instead of evaluating it.
# This is the structural quotability the macro layer wants:
#   quote (1 add 2)      -> 3                 (evaluate, then quote result)
#   codequote (1 add 2)  -> the paren as code (NOT evaluated)
# Words -> atoms and lists -> raw list behave exactly like `quote`.
# Expected values use the canon renderer.
# See design/legacy/PAREN-REPRESENTATION.9.ignore Step 4.
# --- word / scalar / list forms behave like quote ---
codequote foo
column3: bare word -> Atom (data, not a call)

column1: codequote add
column3: works on bound names too (pure data)

column1: codequote 99
codequote [1 add 2]
# --- the new behaviour: a paren is captured RAW as code ---
codequote (1 add 2)
column3: paren captured raw — NOT evaluated to 3

column1: codequote (nosuchword)
column3: contents NOT evaluated — no undefined_word error

column1: # --- guard: quote keeps its evaluate-then-quote semantics (unchanged) ---
quote (1 add 2)
column3: quote still evaluates the paren, then quotes the result
